parts.instruction: Read the passage below and answer Questions 1-2 by selecting the best option.
parts.contentHtml:
The Cognitive Architecture of Multilingual Minds

A. The cognitive benefits of acquiring multiple languages have fascinated neuroscientists and linguists for over a century. Early hypotheses in the mid-twentieth century posited that managing multiple linguistic systems might create cognitive overload or delay primary linguistic milestones. However, contemporary neuroimaging studies employing fMRI and electroencephalography demonstrate the precise opposite: early bilingualism enhances executive attention control and neuroplasticity.

B. In second language acquisition, developmental stages play a pivotal role. Research confirms that childhood immersion fosters native-like phonetic sensitivity and intuitive syntactic processing. As individuals transition into adulthood, language learning relies progressively on deliberate cognitive strategies and explicit grammatical deduction rather than automatic absorption.

C. Furthermore, recent cross-cultural evaluations across universities illustrate that individuals actively alternating between languages develop superior conflict resolution skills and attentional switching metrics, serving as a protective cognitive buffer against neurodegenerative conditions in later life.

Guaranteed international employment without language certification

parts.contentHtml:
Academic Cross-Linguistic Studies in Higher Education

A. A landmark multi-institutional inquiry surveyed 5,200 undergraduates across ten Southeast Asian educational hubs. The primary research vector sought to delineate correlations between dual-medium instructional modalities and scholastic achievement.

B. Contrary to earlier anecdotal claims that monolingual students excel in single-task focus, bilingual cohorts exhibited notable resilience under timed examination constraints, registering higher problem-solving adaptability across analytical domains.

questions.question_text: The research surveyed more than 5,000 students across 10 universities in Southeast Asia.
Monolingual participants scored higher on multitasking and conflict resolution tests.

A. Immersion models subject learners to sustained auditory and communicative demands. Neuroimaging corroborates that structured immersion promotes neural connectivity across anterior and posterior cortical regions.

Community Library Services & Guidelines

A. The Central City Library offers extensive digital and print resources for lifelong learners, students, and research professionals. Membership is complimentary for all local residents and registered full-time students at partner academic institutions.

B. Quiet study pods may be reserved up to seven days in advance through the online portal or directly at the information desk. Audio-visual learning materials, including multimedia language training kits and test preparation software, are accessible in the Digital Media Hub on the second floor.

C. In addition to regular lending services, the library hosts weekly multilingual conversation workshops and guest author seminars designed to foster inclusive cultural exchange.

parts.contentHtml:
Workplace Ergonomics and Remote Productivity

A. Modern ergonomic research emphasizes dynamic postural adjustment rather than prolonged static seating. Ergonomists recommend changing work positions every thirty to forty-five minutes to mitigate musculoskeletal fatigue and maintain optimal cognitive engagement.

B. When configuring a home workstation, monitor height should align directly with eye level to minimize cervical spinal strain. Ambient lighting should be calibrated to avoid screen glare while maintaining adequate contrast for document review.

questions.question_text: Ergonomists recommend remaining completely stationary in one ergonomic chair position for four continuous hours.
The top of the monitor display should ideally be aligned with the user's natural eye level.
